text.p: The prime minister of the Baltic state of Estonia had his interior minister sacked on Tuesday over an investigation into the abuse of official cars, the news agency ETA said.
It quoted the premier's information office as saying Prime Minister Mart Siimann asked for the dismissal of Interior Minister Raivo Sinijarv and that the country's president agreed.
The agency said Siimann blamed Sinijarv for failing properly to investigate the abuse of official vehicles by Interior Ministry officials.

Estonia, which quit the former Soviet Union in 1991, has been through several political crises but the sacking of Sinijarv was not expected to affect the ruling minority government as he is a member of Siimann's own Coalition Party.
